hypothesis: The complete v25 live portfolio can produce mechanically valid protected lifecycles while causal eligible-signal, missed-opportunity, orderbook-alignment, and exit-mechanism telemetry identifies repeatable provider-symbol behavior that clears measured live friction.
decision: Keep the running v25 strategy and its three protected open lifecycles unchanged. Preserve the SOL Hulk target behavior: its first current-run lifecycle realized +$0.681124 net, while the predeclared 25-bps activation and 10-bps trail would have reduced that result by $0.469681. Do not loosen a blocker or make L2 pressure an execution gate from the new positive slices: only two of 53 one-blocker comparisons with at least three non-overlapping paths were positive after the 13-bps estimate, both were SOL long at 60 minutes, and only one of 27 aligned-versus-opposed L2 comparisons with at least three paths per side had positive aligned mean return after friction. Continue measuring the open SOL HT-Breakout lifecycle, ETH precompression lifecycle, and GOLD Swing lifecycle through their actual venue exits before proposing a profile transition.
falsifier: A lifecycle, fill, fee, funding, event-identity, protection, authority, or evidence-hash inconsistency invalidates this prefix. Repeated independent live SOL outcomes showing the tight profit lock improves net results would overturn its current rejection. Repeated positive after-friction one-blocker or L2-aligned outcomes across independent windows would support a separately tested candidate; disappearance of the current positive slices as the window grows would weaken them.
limitations: Two closed current-run trades and eight eligible evaluations are too sparse to estimate durable portfolio edge, income, or drawdown.
The ETH, SOL HT-Breakout, and GOLD lifecycles remain open; their marked PnL, MFE, MAE, and profit-protection states are provisional and excluded from closed performance.
The eight eligible evaluations include overlapping same-market provider observations and are not eight independent trades.
One-blocker and L2 paths assume no orders or fills and subtract an estimated 13-bps round trip; they are opportunity diagnostics rather than executable PnL.
The two positive one-blocker comparisons are 60-minute SOL long slices from one short live window and may represent the same market move rather than two edges.
The 53 one-blocker and 27 L2 comparisons reuse events across routes and horizons; comparison count is not independent trial count.
The tight profit-lock counterfactual reuses the actual exit fill-to-reference ratio and fee rate, so it is mechanism evidence rather than a claim of an executable historical fill.
The v25 process predates staged v27 HIP-3 telemetry repairs, so unavailable HIP-3 entry components cannot be interpreted as repaired-profile behavior.
HT-Breakout is the operator-facing name; the evidence retains the legacy internal strategy identifier for compatibility.
